cmad.notes: No CMAD located. No designated CMAD repository is configured; the provider sites (goes-r.gov and the NOAA NCEI GOES-R space weather pages) offer ReadMe files, user guides, an EXIS L1b algorithms document (CDRL80) and the GOES-R Series Data Book, but no CMAD; web searches for 'GOES-R Calibration and Measurement Algorithms Document' and 'GOES-16 CMAD' found nothing. GOES-16 is a NOAA operational satellite whose flight segment NASA procured on NOAA's behalf; it is not funded through NASA Heliophysics senior review, so a CMAD is not expected and its absence is unremarkable. GOES-16 was also replaced as GOES-East by GOES-19 on 2025-04-07 and is now the on-orbit standby satellite, although the SPASE record has no StopDate. Proceeded with the remaining sources.

instrument_coverage.notes: Reverse lookup: the SMWG clone holds only two Instrument records pointing at spase://SMWG/Observatory/GOES/16 (MAG and Ephemeris); a sweep of every naming authority on spase-metadata.org found four more under the NOAA authority (EXIS, EXIS/EUVS, EXIS/XRS, SUVI), each confirmed to carry ObservatoryID spase://SMWG/Observatory/GOES/16. The external roster comes from the goes-r.gov instruments page (ABI, GLM, EXIS, SUVI, SEISS, MAG), the goes-r.gov SEISS and EXIS pages (SEISS sensors EHIS, MPS-HI, MPS-LO, SGPS; EXIS sensors EUVS and XRS), and the 2017 NTRS space segment overview, whose abstract lists the same six instruments; the sources agree. CCOR is flown only on GOES-U (GOES-19) and is not part of the GOES-16 payload. The communication relay payloads are not science instruments and are not counted. The Ephemeris record is a platform pseudo-instrument (spacecraft position), not a payload instrument, and its Contacts hold only the UNKNOWN placeholder. ABI, GLM and SEISS (with its four sensors) have no SPASE Instrument record; their leads were taken from their description papers and they are listed in pending_instrument_runs. ABI and GLM are Earth-observing (meteorological) instruments.

pending_instrument_runs.notes: Description paper resolved with confidence (Schmit et al. 2017); positions 1-3 (Schmit, Griffith, Gunshor) taken as Strong. An ABI Instrument record would be needed before a per-instrument run.
Description paper resolved with confidence (Goodman et al. 2013); positions 1-3 (Goodman, Blakeslee, Koshak) taken as Strong.

Two suite-level descriptions, both cited on the NOAA NCEI SEISS page: Dichter et al. 2015 (10.1109/TNS.2015.2477997) and Kress et al. 2020 (10.1016/B978-0-12-814327-8.00020-2); leads of both taken at Medium (Dichter, Galica, McGarity; Kress, Rodriguez, Onsager). A same-team conference overview (10.1117/12.2228537) and sensor-level papers cited by NCEI (MPS-HI 10.1029/2019SW002403, SGPS 10.1029/2021SW002750, EHIS angle-detector prototype 10.1016/j.nima.2016.08.038) were not used here. None of the four sensors has a SPASE record.

Three candidate XRS descriptions: Chamberlin et al. 2009 (10.1117/12.826807, design phase), Woods et al. 2024 (10.1029/2024JA032925, design and pre-flight calibration) and Machol et al. 2026 (10.1029/2026JA035181, on-orbit calibration); NCEI cites the latter two. Positions 1-3 of each taken at Medium. Contacts-derived InstrumentScientist (Machol) captured.

notes: Mission overview selection is UNCERTAIN, so its positions 1-3 were taken at Medium and positions 4-5 at Low. No multi-author, peer-reviewed GOES-R mission overview paper was found in Crossref or Semantic Scholar. The overview material is the GOES-R Series reference volume (Elsevier, Oct 2019, cited as 2020; editors Goodman, Schmit, Daniels, Redmon; ISBN 978-0-12-814327-8, whose volume-level DOI 10.1016/C2015-0-06249-1 does not resolve) with its single-author introduction (Goodman) and spacecraft-and-instruments (Sullivan) chapters and its four-author summary chapter (same order as the editors), plus a three-author 2017 EUMETSAT conference overview on NTRS (Sullivan, Krimchansky, Walsh; not peer-reviewed; 2 citations). All fall within the timing window and name GOES-R, but each fails the author-count or peer-review check and several score similarly. Redmon (fourth editor) is included through his magnetometer-paper position instead.
SciX/ADS was not queried because no API token is available in this environment; literature cross-checks used Crossref and Semantic Scholar.

ABI: Schmit et al. 2017 (10.1175/BAMS-D-15-00230.1) selected with confidence: title names ABI and GOES-R, 6 authors, published 2017 (within a year of the start of the operating span), 579 Crossref / 640 Semantic Scholar citations, and both indexes agree on the author list. The 2005 design-phase ABI paper (10.1175/BAMS-86-8-1079) was considered and not selected (11 years before launch). Backward scan: sorted suffix of 3 (Daniels, Goodman, Lebair), so the list is not alphabetized.

GLM: Goodman et al. 2013 (10.1016/j.atmosres.2013.01.006; online 2012) selected with confidence: design-phase description 3.5 years before launch, 11 authors, about 400-480 citations, both indexes agree. The 2020 GLM chapter of the reference volume (10.1016/B978-0-12-814327-8.00016-0) was considered and not selected. Backward scan: sorted suffix of 3 (Bateman, McCaul, Stano), so not alphabetized.

EXIS: Machol et al. 2020 (10.1016/B978-0-12-814327-8.00019-6) selected with confidence as the only suite-level EXIS description found (14 authors, 2020). Backward scan: sorted suffix of 2 (Bouwer, Reinard), so not alphabetized; positions 1-3 = Machol, Eparvier, Viereck.

EUVS: Eparvier et al. 2009 (10.1117/12.826445) selected with confidence as the only whole-sensor EUVS description (later papers cover only the EUVS-C channel or are conference summaries). Backward scan: sorted suffix of 5 (Crotser, Jones, McClintock, Snow, Woods) starting at author 2, so the list is PARTIALLY alphabetized with a prefix of 1; only Eparvier gets position-based evidence. Scope recorded as component (a sensor within the EXIS suite).

XRS: selection UNCERTAIN, with three candidates (Chamberlin et al. 2009; Woods et al. 2024 and Machol et al. 2026, the two cited by NCEI). The 2024 and 2026 papers fall well outside the 2-5 year window, but they are the ones the provider cites. Positions 1-3 of each were taken at Medium. None of the lists is alphabetized (sorted suffixes of 2, 2 and 3). Author-order discrepancy for Woods et al. 2024: Semantic Scholar places Eden last, but the publisher's Crossref record and both ESSOAr preprint versions place him second; the Crossref order was used.

SUVI: Darnel et al. 2022 (10.1029/2022SW003044) selected with confidence: title names SUVI, 16 authors including the Lockheed Martin builder team, 43 Crossref citations, both indexes agree. Timing is borderline (April 2022, about 5.4 years after the start of the operating span). Considered and not selected: the builder's 2019 SPIE design and on-orbit calibration paper (Vasudevan et al. 2019, 10.1117/12.2536196; 6 citations), the reference-volume SUVI chapter (Seaton et al. 2020, 10.1016/B978-0-12-814327-8.00018-4), and a 2010 SPIE telescope design paper (10.1117/12.864577). Backward scan: sorted suffix of 3 (Edwards, Mathur, Timothy), so not alphabetized.

MAG: Loto'aniu et al. 2019 (10.1007/s11214-019-0600-3) selected with confidence: title names GOES-16 and the magnetometer, 15 authors, published 2.5 years after launch, peer-reviewed, both indexes agree. Backward scan: sorted suffix of 4 (Chu, Early, Kronenwetter, Todirita), below the 5-name threshold, so the list is not alphabetized. MAG authors 5-15 appear with initials only.

SEISS: selection UNCERTAIN. NCEI cites two suite-level descriptions, the builder's 2015 IEEE TNS paper (46 Crossref citations) and the NOAA reference-volume chapter (37 citations); they score similarly, so the leads of both were taken at Medium. The builder's 2016 SPIE overview (10.1117/12.2228537) is a same-team companion to the 2015 paper, is not cited by NCEI, and was not treated as a separate description. Neither list is alphabetized.

On this Observatory run each instrument paper contributes positions 1-3 only; authors at position 4 or later are excluded as instrument-team depth unless an independent source includes them (Goodman and Daniels on the ABI paper, Singer on the MAG paper, and several EXIS/XRS/SUVI authors who lead another paper).

GOES-R Program team page: only Daniel Lindsey holds a qualifying title (Program Scientist). The other nine programme-office staff hold management or administrative titles, which are non-qualifying, and are excluded. Lindsey is taken to be the Daniel T. Lindsey who wrote the reference-volume RGB chapter; the team page gives no middle initial.

Goodman's ProgramScientist role rests on the title 'GOES-R Program Chief Scientist' on his 2015 presentation slide. A search-result summary of his NESDIS biography (the page returned HTTP 403) describes him as GOES-R Senior Program Scientist from 2007 to 2017, retiring in 2017; that text was not read directly.

Sullivan's GOES-R titles (NASA Flight Project manager, then NOAA System Program Director) are management roles and non-qualifying; she is included only through overview authorship. Krimchansky and Walsh are included only through the 2017 NTRS conference overview. A reviewer should decide whether space-segment engineering and management leads belong on the observatory DOI.

Howard J. Singer is PI of the GOES-16 MAG only in the 2019 SMWG Instrument record (SPASE Version 2.3.0), which may be out of date. The description paper is led by Loto'aniu, and Singer is its fourth author. A reviewer should confirm who currently leads GOES-R MAG science.

Person-registry issues: Robert Redmon has two Person records (Robert.J.Redmon and Robert.Redmon); Robert.J.Redmon was used. Dichter has Bronislaw.K.Dichter (ATC, 2.7.1) and a legacy B.Dichter (Panametrics, 2.2.0); Bronislaw.K.Dichter was used. Several records carry stale affiliations (Steven.J.Goodman: NASA MSFC; Rodney.Viereck: USAF Phillips Laboratory). Terrance G. Onsager is matched to Terry.Onsager. Matches for initials-only MAG authors (W. Rowland to William.F.Rowland; F. J. Rich to Frederick.J.Rich) and for Steven M. Hill (Steven.Hill) and Andrew R. Jones (Andrew.Jones) rest on initials and affiliation and should be verified.

Record hygiene for curators: the Observatory record's only Contact is the spase://SMWG/Person/UNKNOWN placeholder (GeneralContact), as is the Ephemeris record's PrincipalInvestigator; the NSSDC Master Catalog InformationURL currently returns an NSSDCA error page; the Wikipedia InformationURL name misspells 'Wikipedia'; the Description refers to 'GOES 17' inside the GOES-16 record; and the record carries no StopDate although GOES-16 left GOES-East service on 2025-04-07 and is now on-orbit standby.

The GOES-R Series reference volume's Contributors list (about 70 names) is participation-level evidence and is not listed individually. The volume's ABI-application, product and data-access chapters are not instrument or mission descriptions and were not used.

ABI and GLM are Earth-observing instruments. Their leads (Schmit, Griffith, Gunshor; Goodman, Blakeslee, Koshak) are included because the Observatory record describes the whole GOES-16 spacecraft. A reviewer should decide whether a heliophysics-registry observatory DOI should carry them.
The NOAA-authority EXIS, EUVS and XRS Instrument records were released on 2026-09-17 and are not in the SMWG clone; they were read from hpde/NOAA on GitHub.
